newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. asks agencies to keep spending, avoid layoffs.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. asks agencies to keep spending, avoid layoffs.

text.p: The New York state budget director has asked agencies not to spend more in the coming 1997-1998 fiscal year than in the previous year, but in a new move, added they also should not seek to layoff more workers.

"Your request should reflect a continued effort to reorganize your agency's operations and finances -- including combining or eliminating programs where appropriate -- to advance the governor's goal of making state government more efficient and responsive," said Patricia Woodworth, in a letter dated September 20.
"You should assume that the strict hiring freeze will continue through 1997-98 and your request should not propose layoffs."

Since the Pataki Administration took office, the ranks of state workers have been cut by about 20,000 to 191,000, but state officials said the decision not to seek more reductions does not mean the end of its efforts to cut expenses.

"I think costs are going to have to be cut, but clearly there are not going to be any reductions in the budget recommendations from agencies," said a state official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

A spokesman for Governor George Pataki said it was premature to comment on the likely shape of the next fiscal budget. Some Republican state legislators who now are running for re-election in the Albany region, which has borne the brunt of the cutbacks because it is the capital, applauded the decision to stop laying off workers.
"Now we are turning the corner and using our talented workforce to find ways to make government run more efficiently," said Michale Hoblock, R-Colonie, in prepared remarks.

Saying that layoffs had been kept to an "absolute minimum," Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, D-Troy, said: "I hope the directive that state agencies should not propose any layoffs will silence the chorus of naysayers who've been predicting tens of thousands of layoffs that never came about." Bruno made the comment prepared remarks.
